elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "no such approval shall be required for an assignment to an affiliate" (with "financially responsible" qualifier deleted)

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "No approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets."

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, which is not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights ... without the prior written approval of the other party" + "Client's approval of an assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall have no right to terminate this Agreement upon a change of control of Client."

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Successor carve-out runs one way only: "an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"
No notice mechanic appears anywhere in the revised clause

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Client's approval of an assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All five preferred atomic elements are present in operative text: Customer affiliate assignment free of consent, Customer successor carve-out for merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets, reasonableness standard on Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment, an absolute bar on Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor, and an express denial of any Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.

The fallback is not independently satisfied (successor right is one-directional and no written-notice mechanic was added), but that is irrelevant because the locked preferred level is complete; the two levels were not mixed.
Edits are confined to a two-word deletion plus one concise inserted sentence group; no boilerplate, no whole-clause rewrite, no new exceptions, and no offending surplus wording.

Residual note only (not a deviation): the pre-existing mutual affiliate exception still lets Vendor assign to its own affiliate without Customer approval, and deleting "financially responsible" marginally widens that reciprocal right; the preferred position's Vendor-consent requirement otherwise stands.
No undefined terms or dangling mechanics: "Client" and "TrueLink" are the defined parties and the untouched consent sentence remains fully effective.
